subject: [PATCH] NFSD: Reject a COPY whose source and destination are the same file

reviews.author: Chuck Lever
reviews.summary: Applied the patch to nfsd-testing without raising any concerns.
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:42:56 -0800, Jeff Layton wrote:
> RFC 7862 Section 15.2.3 says that COPY MUST fail with NFS4ERR_INVAL
> when SAVED_FH and CURRENT_FH refer to the same file, whatever the
> ranges. NFSD never checks for this. A same-file COPY with
> non-overlapping ranges succeeds, and one with overlapping ranges fails
> only because the VFS rejects it.
> 
> The overlap-only rule applies to CLONE (Section 15.13.3), so leave
> nfsd4_verify_copy() alone. Instead, check in nfsd4_setup_intra_ssc(),
> after both stateids are verified. For an inter-server copy, SAVED_FH
> names a file on another server, so that path is not affected.
> 
> [...]

Applied to nfsd-testing, thanks!

[1/1] NFSD: Reject a COPY whose source and destination are the same file
      commit: c235ae9d5057e37ed83de15b27fd8b8174a032d0

--
Chuck Lever <cel@kernel.org>

2026-11-19.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NFSD (Network File System Daemon) to reject COPY operations when the source and destination files are the same, as per RFC 7862 Section 15.2.3. The existing implementation never checked for this condition, leading to potential issues with overlapping ranges. The change is made in nfsd4_setup_intra_ssc() by adding a check for identical file inodes.

reviews.author: Aurélien Couderc
reviews.summary: Raised concerns about the restriction on same-file COPY operations, suggesting it may be too restrictive and potentially break existing use cases.
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu, Nov 19, 2026 at 6:44 PM Jeff Layton <jlayton@kernel.org> wrote:
>
> RFC 7862 Section 15.2.3 says that COPY MUST fail with NFS4ERR_INVAL
> when SAVED_FH and CURRENT_FH refer to the same file, whatever the
> ranges. NFSD never checks for this. A same-file COPY with
> non-overlapping ranges succeeds, and one with overlapping ranges fails
> only because the VFS rejects it.
>
> The overlap-only rule applies to CLONE (Section 15.13.3), so leave
> nfsd4_verify_copy() alone. Instead, check in nfsd4_setup_intra_ssc(),
> after both stateids are verified. For an inter-server copy, SAVED_FH
> names a file on another server, so that path is not affected.
>
> The Linux client never sends a same-file COPY, so this does not change
> its behaviour. Found by pynfs COPY11.

Why should COPY within the same file be blocked?

For example: Windows FSCTL_OFFLOAD_READ+FSCTL_OFFLOAD_WRITE is used
exactly like that by databases like Oracle. Even advertised as a
"database accelerator" feature...

Better tix the NFSv4.2 COPY spec at RFC level then...

Aurélien
-- 
Aurélien Couderc <aurelien.couderc2002@gmail.com>
Big Data/Data mining expert, chess enthusiast

> > 
> > The Linux client never sends a same-file COPY, so this does not change
